SEA.head: The matchup suits the Kraken
SEA.body: Seattle has home-ice advantage and has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Canucks can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

VAN.head: Not an easy night for the Canucks
VAN.body: Seattle has home-ice advantage and has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Canucks’ best way through is a power play that gets going.

story.head: Oleksiak returns to Seattle
paras: The Kraken are on a three-game losing streak, while the Canucks have won two in a row. Going in, the Canucks are last in the NHL and the Kraken sixth in the Pacific (tied for 25th in the NHL).

The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.239) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .332, mostly because they’re 3-5 in one-goal games. The Kraken’s record (.528) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.399), largely thanks to their finishing.

This season, the Kraken have been outscored 66-57, even though they’ve outscored teams 43-40 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 19-12, and no team allows more chances on the penalty kill.

The Canucks have had shaky goaltending (32nd), have a leaky penalty kill (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). Vancouver has allowed 4.35 goals a game, the most in the league. As for the Kraken, they roll their lines more evenly than almost anyone (2nd), rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd) and give up a lot of shots (32nd). The Kraken keep dangerous shots away, but the Canucks give up a lot of them.

Brock Boeser (8 G / 15 A / 23 P in 23 GP) is tied for the Canucks’ scoring lead, with eight points in his last five games. Elias Pettersson (#40) (6 G / 17 A / 23 P in 23 GP) shares it. For the Kraken, Berkly Catton (5 G / 9 A / 14 P in 18 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Frédérick Gaudreau (8 G / 3 A / 11 P in 18 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Leevi Meriläinen (3-9-1 / .888 SV% in 14 GS) is expected to start for Vancouver, and Joey Daccord (4-4-0 / .872 SV% in 9 GS) for Seattle.

items.text: Jamie Oleksiak faces Seattle for the first time since leaving.

The Canucks have been without Thatcher Demko all season. Leevi Meriläinen is expected to start.
Frédérick Gaudreau has seven goals on chances worth about 3.0 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
